Vancouver, Canada, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Clearmind Medicine Inc. (Nasdaq: CMND) (“Clearmind” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing non-hallucinogenic psychedelic-derived neuroplastogens for scalable treatment of neuropsychiatric, metabolic, and addiction disorders including Alcohol Use Disorder (“AUD”), today announced the publication of a Hong Kong patent application covering innovative psychedelic compounds targeting the treatment of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (“PTSD”) and other mental health disorders.

The patent application is part of the Company's exclusive worldwide licensing agreement with Yissum Research Development Company of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (“Yissum”). The compounds were invented by Professors Ahmed Masaewa, Rami Yaka, and Avi Priel of the Hebrew University. Under the licensing agreement, Clearmind holds exclusive global rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize the novel compounds.

The Hong Kong patent publication expands Clearmind's global patent application portfolio for its proprietary PTSD-focused psychedelic compounds. Together with existing international filings, the application supports the Company's strategy to seek intellectual property protection for its novel therapeutic candidates across major global markets.

According to market research by Heimdall Insights, the global PTSD therapeutics market was valued at approximately $19 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $24.8 billion by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 5.5%. In addition, GlobalData projects that the PTSD pharmaceutical market across seven major markets is projected to grow from $1.2 billion in 2024 to $5.5 billion by 2034, at a CAGR of 16.1%,  reflecting anticipated demand for innovative treatment options.

About Clearmind Medicine Inc.

Clearmind is a clinical-stage neuroplastogens pharmaceutical biotech company focused on the discovery and development of non-hallucinogenic, second generation, neuroplastogen-derived therapeutics to solve widespread and underserved health problems, including alcohol use disorder. Its primary objective is to research and develop psychedelic-based compounds and attempt to commercialize them as regulated medicines, foods, or supplements.

The Company’s intellectual property portfolio currently consists of nineteen patent families, including 32 granted patents. The Company intends to seek additional patents for its compounds whenever warranted and will remain opportunistic regarding the acquisition of additional intellectual property to build its portfolio.

Shares of Clearmind are listed for trading on Nasdaq under the symbol "CMND."

CEO Leandro Iglesias outlines three drivers for 2027: the proposed Ultranet acquisition, the Q1 2027 commercial launch of IQSTEL Digital's microdrama service, and a step-up in profitability and cash generation across the platform.

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

Letter to Shareholders

November 19, 2026

Dear Shareholders,

I believe 2027 will be the most important year in IQSTEL's history. Much of what we built in 2026 was designed to set up what comes next: a larger and more profitable telecom platform, a new stream of recurring digital revenue, and a clear path toward consolidated positive cash flow.

Our accomplishments in 2026 have built strong momentum as we head into 2027. Through the first nine months of 2026, we generated $313.0 million in consolidated revenue, up 34.5% from the same period in 2025. We completed the first financing tranche intended to support our proposed acquisition of Ultranet. And on November 10, our first mobile operator partner approved the start of integration for IQSTEL Digital's microdrama service, which we are targeting for commercial launch in the first quarter of 2027.

Each of these milestones points to the same objective: use the scale and commercial reach of our telecom business to deliver stronger margins, cash generation and recurring revenue. Here is how we intend to do that in 2027.

The interconnections, integrations and billing relationships we have developed with more than 600 telecommunications operators in 24 countries give us established channels to introduce higher-margin services without building distribution from scratch. In 2027, our focus is to put those channels to work.

Ultranet: a step-change in scale and cash generation

IQSTEL Digital: 2027 is our launch year

IQSTEL Digital is how we intend to turn the reach of our operator network into recurring, higher-margin revenue. The first operator's network serves approximately 14 million subscribers. Under our planning assumptions, it could support up to 105,000 active paid monthly microdrama subscriptions. Reaching our 2027 objective of 300,000 active paid monthly subscriptions will depend on adding operators from our initial outreach group and beyond, as well as on integration, operator execution and customer demand.

At 300,000 subscriptions, our illustrative model indicates $1.8 million to $3.6 million in annualized profit contribution. Our plan is to launch, measure results with our first operator, and use what we learn as the template for expanding across our operator relationships. Over the longer term, we see Digital Services as the primary driver of our path toward a $15 million Operating Adjusted EBITDA run rate.

Our priorities for 2027

Our team is focused on five priorities:

Finish 2026 strongly. Close the year with a strong fourth quarter as we work toward our $430 million revenue objective.

Close and integrate Ultranet. Complete the definitive agreement and closing on acceptable terms, then integrate Ultranet's profitable operations into our platform.

Launch and scale IQSTEL Digital. Go live with our first operator in Q1 2027, add operators through the year, and work toward 300,000 active paid monthly subscriptions.

Turn scale into margins and cash flow. Raise our Operating Adjusted EBITDA run rate and advance our goal of consolidated positive cash flow.

Keep shareholders informed. Report our progress against these objectives clearly and consistently, and expand our engagement with the investment community throughout the year.

As part of that engagement, I invite you to review Edison Investment Research's latest note on IQSTEL, "Another steady step forward in Q326," published on November 18, 2026 following our third-quarter results. Edison highlights our sustained organic growth, the continued operating profitability of our Telecom business and our balance sheet, and notes that the IQSTEL Digital launch remains on track for the first quarter of 2027. After adjusting its 2026 estimates for the Ultranet closing now expected in the first quarter of 2027, Edison left its 2027 and 2028 forecasts and its $6 per share valuation assessment unchanged. The full note and Edison's September 2026 initiation report are available on our Investor Relations website at https://ir.iqstel.com/analyst-coverage. IQSTEL is a research client of Edison and paid for the research; Edison's forecasts and valuation are its own and should not be read as Company guidance.

We have built a business with substantial scale. 2027 is about converting that scale into higher margins, recurring digital revenue, cash generation and lasting value for our shareholders. I am confident in our direction and in the team executing this plan.

Thank you for your continued confidence in IQSTEL and in the people working to deliver this next phase of our growth.

Sincerely,

Leandro Iglesias

IQSTEL Inc. (NASDAQ: IQST) is a global telecommunications and technology company operating through two core business divisions: Telecom and Digital Services. The Telecom Division is the foundation of IQSTEL's global platform, operating across 20 countries with more than 600 telecommunications carrier interconnections and delivering international voice, SMS, messaging, and connectivity solutions to some of the world's largest telecom operators and enterprise customers. Through these customer relationships, IQSTEL's platform has the potential to reach approximately 2.3 billion end users worldwide. Building on this global infrastructure and commercial reach, the Digital Services Division is focused on higher-margin technology solutions across Content Services, Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Communications, Cybersecurity, Fintech, and Enterprise Automation. Dublin, Ireland, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Fusion Fuel Green PLC (Nasdaq: HTOO) (“Fusion Fuel” or the “Company”), a diversified energy platform, today announced that it is evaluating potential investment opportunities in Venezuela, with an initial focus on energy, natural resources and related infrastructure. Through its subsidiary Royal Uranium Inc. (“Royal Uranium”), the Company already holds a portfolio of uranium and natural gas royalty and other interests. In Venezuela, the Company is exploring potential royalty interests, joint ventures or other commercial arrangements, and acquisitions. Management believes that Venezuela’s resource base, increasing oil production and evolving investment framework may create long-term investment opportunities.

Evaluation of Potential Investments

The Company is in preliminary discussions with multiple parties regarding specific investment opportunities. Potential transaction structures include royalty interests, joint ventures or other commercial arrangements, and acquisitions of local businesses. The Company has not entered into any definitive agreement with respect to any such opportunity. The Company intends to focus on opportunities with identifiable assets, risk-adjusted economics that it considers acceptable and a clear strategic fit, and expects to provide updates as material developments occur. Any such transaction would extend the Company’s strategy of acquiring royalty and other interests beyond the jurisdictions in which Royal Uranium currently holds interests.

Venezuela’s Oil and Gas Resources

Venezuela’s oil production has recovered from historic lows in recent years. In 2020, Venezuela’s crude oil production fell as low as approximately 340,000 barrels per day, according to OPEC data. OPEC secondary sources estimate that production averaged approximately 1.15 million barrels per day in September 2026, more than three times that low, while Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. (“PDVSA”), Venezuela’s state oil company, reported that daily production reached 1.252 million barrels on October 23, 2026. Output nonetheless remains well below the more than 3 million barrels per day that Venezuela produced in the late 1990s, and certain analysts estimate that restoring production to historical levels will require approximately $100 billion or more in investment. Venezuela also holds approximately 195 trillion cubic feet (approximately 5.5 trillion cubic meters) of proven natural gas reserves, representing approximately 73% of South America’s total, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Legal and Regulatory Developments

Recent legal and regulatory developments have also opened a path for new private investment in Venezuela. In January 2026, Venezuela amended its Organic Hydrocarbons Law to permit privately owned companies domiciled in Venezuela to carry out upstream oil and associated gas activities under contracts with wholly state-owned companies, providing an alternative to the prior regime, under which private participation in upstream activities was generally limited to minority interests in state-controlled joint ventures. Since January 2026, the U.S. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”) has issued a series of general licenses that, among other things, permit the negotiation of and entry into contingent contracts for new investment in Venezuela’s oil, gas, petrochemical and electricity sectors and, under a separate general license, its minerals sector, with performance of those contracts subject to separate OFAC authorization. International energy companies, including Chevron, Repsol and Shell, have entered into new agreements or expanded their activities in Venezuela, and in November 2026 ExxonMobil signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and PDVSA to evaluate potential upstream opportunities, almost two decades after leaving the country.

Against this backdrop, Fusion Fuel believes Venezuela may offer investment opportunities in energy, natural resources and related infrastructure. In its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, the International Monetary Fund projects that Venezuela’s real GDP will grow by approximately 5% in 2026.

Local Knowledge and a Disciplined Investment Approach

Members of Fusion Fuel’s senior team have long-standing personal ties to Venezuela and on-the-ground knowledge of its market and business community. The team also has relationships with international investors seeking exposure to Venezuela’s economic recovery.

“We believe the changes in Venezuela’s legal and regulatory framework may create long-term investment opportunities for Fusion Fuel,” said Frederico Figueira de Chaves, Chief Executive Officer of Fusion Fuel. “In 2026, Venezuela amended its hydrocarbons law, the U.S. issued licenses permitting companies to negotiate contingent contracts for new investment, and international energy companies have expanded their activities in the country or are evaluating a return. We intend to evaluate these opportunities in a disciplined manner, consistent with our strategy of building a diversified energy platform, and to pursue only those that we believe have the potential to create value for our shareholders.”

Any transaction would be subject to due diligence, definitive transaction documentation, any required regulatory authorizations, and compliance with applicable sanctions and other laws in each jurisdiction relevant to Fusion Fuel, including U.S. and EU sanctions, and there can be no assurance that any transaction will be entered into or completed.

About Fusion Fuel Green PLC

Fusion Fuel Green PLC (Nasdaq: HTOO) is a diversified energy platform offering a comprehensive suite of energy supply, distribution, and engineering and advisory solutions through its operating businesses Al Shola Al Modea Gas Distribution L.L.C. (“Al Shola Gas”), Bright Hydrogen Solutions Ltd (“BrightHy Solutions”) and Biosteam Energy (Proprietary) Limited (“BioSteam Energy”). Al Shola Gas provides full-service industrial liquefied petroleum gas (“LPG”) solutions, including the design, supply, and maintenance of LPG systems, as well as the transport and distribution of LPG across commercial, industrial, and residential sectors. BrightHy Solutions, the Company’s hydrogen solutions platform, delivers engineering and advisory services enabling decarbonization across hard-to-abate industries. BioSteam Energy provides biomass-powered industrial steam solutions to clients. Through Royal Uranium Inc., the Company also holds a portfolio of uranium and natural gas royalty and other interests across Canada, Colombia and Argentina. SAN ANTONIO, TX / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Valion Bio, Inc. (NASDAQ:VBIO) ("Valion" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing biologics that activate innate immune pathways for cytoprotection and immune modulation, today announced that Armand Balboni, JD, MD, PhD, has become an Advisor on Valion's scientific strategy and medical countermeasure development efforts, with a focus on advancing Entolimod and pursuing government and strategic partnerships.

The advisory role brings together scientific, regulatory, and military medical expertise as Valion Bio prepares for a key development milestone for Entolimod, it's lead medical countermeasure candidate. Entolimod is currently advancing through a therapeutic efficacy study evaluating survival and gastrointestinal recovery following radiation exposure.

"Armand's experience spans several of the capabilities central to advancing Entolimod: drug development, regulatory execution, military medical requirements and procurement, and strategic partnerships," said Dean Zikria, Valion's Interim Chief Executive Officer. "His mandate is to lead our scientific strategy and pursue government and industry partnerships to advance Entolimod toward its next development milestones."

"After a career spent on both the government and industry sides of medical countermeasure development, I was selective about where to go next," said Dr. Balboni. "Valion stood out: a candidate with Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations, fully funded safety and therapeutic efficacy studies, and a clear regulatory pathway under the FDA's Animal Rule. That combination is rare, and I am excited to help Dean and the team advance Entolimod."

Dr. Balboni brings extensive experience spanning biotechnology, clinical drug development, military medicine, regulatory affairs, and strategic partnerships. He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of Appili Therapeutics Inc., where he led corporate strategy, clinical development, and regulatory activities, including oversight of a 1,500-patient Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating an antiviral treatment for COVID-19.

During his distinguished military career, including 24 years of service, Dr. Balboni held senior leadership positions across the U.S. Army, including Deputy Director of the Office of Regulated Activities (ORA), where he helped oversee Food and Drug Administration ("FDA")-regulated clinical trials involving drugs, biologics, and medical devices. His responsibilities included regulatory submissions, emergency use authorization activities, agency interactions, and the evaluation and procurement of medical technologies supporting military requirements.

Dr. Balboni also completed a Department of Defense fellowship at the FDA, serving in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research and the Office of Counterterrorism and Emerging Threats. Previously, at the U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID), he directed technology transfer and strategic collaborations with universities, government agencies, and biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies.

His experience also includes serving as principal investigator on a federally funded vaccine development program targeting pneumonic tularemia, as well as academic leadership and teaching positions at the United States Air Force Academy, the United States Military Academy at West Point, and other institutions. He completed doctoral studies at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and earned his law degree from Brooklyn Law School.

About Valion Bio, Inc.

Valion Bio, Inc. (NASDAQ:VBIO) is developing biologics that activate innate immune pathways for cytoprotection and modulate immune responses in conditions driven by radiation, disease and immune dysregulation.

The Company's lead candidate, Entolimod, is being developed as a potential medical countermeasure for Acute Radiation Syndrome ("ARS") and has been evaluated in animal models under the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's ("FDA") Animal Rule, which allows the Agency to approve new drugs and biological products based on animal efficacy studies when human clinical trials are not ethical or feasible, such as in the case of acute radiation exposure. Entolimod is a novel Toll-like Receptor 5 agonist designed to activate NF-κB signaling pathways associated with cellular protection, tissue recovery and immune response. The product candidate has received Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations from the FDA. Valion holds an exclusive, worldwide license from Statera Biopharma to develop and commercialize Entolimod for ARS, radiation-induced neutropenia, and other indications.

Valion is also advancing Entolasta, a next-generation TLR5 agonist designed for potential use in broader therapeutic applications, including oncology supportive care. The Company's pipeline includes potential programs in neutropenia and immune dysfunction.

Valion's wholly owned subsidiary, Velocity Bioworks, is a biologics contract development and manufacturing organization with mammalian and microbial capabilities, focused on increasing manufacturing control, reducing costs, accelerating development timelines, and strengthening domestic supply-chain security.

HONG KONG, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- 3 E Network Technology Group Limited (Nasdaq: MASK) (the “Company” or “3 E Network”), a business-to-business (“B2B”) information technology (“IT”) business solutions provider committed to becoming a next-generation artificial intelligence (“AI”) infrastructure solutions provider, today announced the extension of its Embodied AI technology applications, officially entering the B2B industrial automation and intralogistics sector. The Company has initiated a R&D program for a heterogeneous compute foundation specifically designed for industrial logistics robotics, including heavy-payload Autonomous Mobile Robots, Automated Guided Vehicles, and autonomous forklift systems. This technological framework encompasses the microarchitecture design of an Edge AI SoC (“System on Chip”) alongside a cloud-based Digital Twin hardware-software collaborative infrastructure. Leveraging foundational logistics network partnerships recently established with industry peers such as Zhengguangtong Logistics, the Company is progressively commencing early-stage commercial Proof of Concept (“PoC”) validation in selected physical intralogistics hubs and warehousing nodes. This development reflects 3 E Network’s “Scenario-Defined Silicon” R&D model, aligning the technological roadmap with practical industrial operational environments during the early stages of underlying computing development.

Advancing Edge AI SoC Microarchitecture Definition through Real-World Data Feedback

In heavy industrial warehousing environments with unstructured elements and frequent human-machine interactions, logistics robotic systems face specific technical requirements regarding millisecond-level dynamic obstacle avoidance, recognition of complex heavy-duty pallets, and trajectory planning in constrained spaces. Current robotic compute architectures typically rely on cloud networks for data exchange and command dispatch. However, in physical environments dense with metallic shelving, centralized architectures face risks of radio frequency signal attenuation and network blind spots, which may lead to system response delays and associated operational safety issues.

To address this industry context, 3 E Network is advancing the Architecture Definition and System-Level Simulation of its Edge AI SoC, designed for Embodied AI. Diverging from traditional, closed semiconductor R&D processes, the Company plans to introduce heterogeneous computing prototype platforms directly into industrial intralogistics nodes for environmental testing. These platforms will incorporate preliminary Spatial Intelligence algorithms and multi-modal sensory arrays, including high-line-count 3D LiDAR and depth-sensing units.

This testing aims to acquire Long-tail Data Distributions and Corner Cases from the physical edge in real time, such as dynamic payload fluctuations, intersections with sightline obstructions between heterogeneous equipment, and visual algorithm variances under non-uniform lighting conditions. These physical data samples from logistics environments will be input into the Company’s system-level simulation platform to verify and optimize the Heterogeneous Computing architecture of the SoC. Based on this feedback, the R&D team is defining the microarchitecture specifications and the underlying Instruction Set Architecture of the built-in multi-modal vision processing engine to establish a system-level balance among general-purpose compute allocation, Memory Bandwidth and Data Throughput Hierarchy, and Neural Processing Unit power efficiency. This data-driven R&D path is intended to ensure that the subsequent silicon physical design meets the specific technical metrics for performance per watt and edge computing capacity (“TOPS”) required in the industrial logistics sector.

Developing an Edge-Cloud Collaborative AI Algorithmic Evolution Platform and Digital Twin System

As the advancement of the underlying edge computing microarchitecture definition, 3 E Network is developing a complementary full-stack ecosystem of “underlying chip + algorithmic evolutionary infrastructure”, initiating R&D for an Edge-Cloud Collaborative AI Digital Twin Infrastructure.

This software ecosystem is architecturally positioned as the cloud-based collaborative network and algorithmic iteration platform for 3 E Network’s upcoming Edge AI compute clusters, serving as a foundational complement to existing application-layer Warehouse Control Systems. Utilizing sensor nodes preliminarily deployed in logistics hubs, this platform focuses on the uplink acquisition and synchronization of data from the physical world. Supported by cloud compute clusters, the infrastructure aims to build a Digital Twin space integrating physics engines, fluid dynamics simulations, and dynamic friction parameters.

Within this 3D virtual environment mapped to physical reality, the Company plans to conduct fine-tuning of Vision-Language-Action Models, Reinforcement Learning, and the iteration of Multi-Agent Collaboration algorithms under complex constraints. Furthermore, the platform introduces an industrial-grade “Shadow Testing” mechanism. Upon the readiness of the Company’s Edge AI SoC for scalable deployment, the Company plans to use this cloud infrastructure to silently dispatch cloud-verified trajectory planning and obstacle avoidance models to physical devices via an Over-The-Air mechanism for background parallel comparison, assuming control only after verifying system-level safety redundancies. This operational loop, which encompasses edge data acquisition, cloud twin training, and edge model updates, will serve as the underlying technical support for the Company to explore the data iteration cycle (“Data Flywheel”).

Defining the Path for Technology Application and Underlying Ecosystem Construction

The announcement of entering intralogistics scenarios and initiating preliminary PoC validation further clarifies 3 E Network’s long-term technology planning in the industrial automation sector. The Company emphasizes its business positioning as a core upstream supplier of underlying technology (“Tier-1 Technology Provider”), dedicated to providing foundational technical support to partners across the supply chain, avoiding direct participation in the commoditized competition of the downstream hardware assembly market.

Addressing the current conditions faced by traditional logistics Original Equipment Manufacturers (“OEMs”) during intelligence transformation, such as high Sunk R&D Costs, substantial algorithm validation Capital Expenditures, and lengthy adaptation cycles for underlying computer chips, 3 E Network plans to explore offering a system-level Turnkey Reference Solution following the completion of current algorithm convergence, hardware simulation validation, and subsequent silicon mass production. This solution is expected to include Edge Compute Ecosystem Access and Cloud Digital Twin System Support for logistics equipment enterprises and supply chain operators.

This commercial structure uses hardware infrastructure as an access point and provides continuous underlying support via cloud systems, intending to assist downstream OEMs in shortening the Time-to-Market for AI systems and optimizing marginal R&D costs. Concurrently, coupling the terminal devices’ perception and control systems with the cloud collaborative network supports the formation of a stable cooperative ecosystem. From a medium-to-long-term business perspective, leveraging the hardware-software collaborative strategy, the Company plans to explore enterprise IT service models, including technology IP licensing and system-level platform access, thereby expanding the Company’s technology application matrix and steadily exploring diversified business models within the B2B market.

Management Commentary

Dr. Tingjun Yang, Chief Executive Officer of 3 E Network, stated: “Physical intralogistics and warehousing networks with high throughput and operational complexity serve as representative testing environments for evaluating the robustness of next generation AI infrastructure systems and the reliability of Embodied AI underlying architectures. Today, we announced the expansion of our R&D direction into the industrial logistics sector, placing algorithm validation nodes into the operational flow of physical supply chains during the initial microarchitecture definition phase of the edge compute framework to execute data-driven concept validations. This action aligns with 3 E Network’s operational principle of building an edge-cloud collaborative architecture that corresponds closely with practical industry demands, focusing on resolving specific technical difficulties in edge autonomous decision-making and heterogeneous multi-agent collaboration for physical industries.”

Dr. Yang pointed out: “Data-driven and hardware-software collaborative design is an important path for technology enterprises to achieve cross-domain technological applications in the AI industrialization process. Management’s current execution focus is on concentrating resources to advance the system-level simulation convergence of the new Edge AI SoC and the code-level deployment of the Digital Twin infrastructure. We will maintain an objective and steady R&D pace, committed to converting our technical accumulation in physical hardware foundations and system-level algorithmic layers into mature technological products, with the expectation of creating sustained corporate value for our clients, the industry, and long-term investors.”

It upholds the industry consensus of “AI and energy symbiosis” and has a strong vision in the field of energy investment. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - V Ten Metals Corp. (TSXV: VTEN) (OTCQB: VTNMF) ("VTen" or the "Company") is pleased to report results from a 183-sample ultrafine soil geochemical survey at EL 23848 on the Company's Tanami Property (the "Property"), located in the Tanami District of the Northern Territory, Australia. The Property consists of four semi-contiguous granted exploration licenses ("ELs") EL 23848, EL 31402, EL 23874 and EL 23875, covering 1,237 sq km located in the Tanami Desert approximately 450km directly northwest of Alice Springs, Northern Territory, Australia.

VTen Metals Delivers First Rare Earth Dataset at Tanami Property and Identifies New Gold-Pathfinder and Ni-Cu-PGE-Style Targets in Previously Untested Basement

Samples were collected at 400 m spacing along nine lines about 2.5 km apart, crossing the Billabong Complex, an Archean basement inlier at the boundary of the Tanami Region and the Aileron Province, to test for hydrothermal unconformity-related REE mineralisation by analogy with Wolverine and Gambit at Browns Range, Western Australia. The survey returned the first rare earth element (REE) data from the property and identified two further targets for styles of mineralisation not previously recognised on the tenement. REE mineralisation reported at other Tanami unconformities is not necessarily indicative of mineralisation at EL 23848.

Highlights

  • First REE data on the property: 183 samples analysed for 65 elements including REE, Au, Pd and Pt; no REE analyses had previously been undertaken on EL 23848.

  • New gold-pathfinder target (T1): arsenic-tellurium-molybdenum zoning into antimony, with palladium, over about 2.8 km of the western line, in granite-gneiss terrain previously explored only for orogenic gold.

  • New Ni-Cu-PGE-style target (T2): copper, sulphur and palladium beside a chromium-nickel peak over about 800 m, with the longest heavy-REE-leaning run in the survey.

Blair Way notes: "this first dataset gives us a geochemical baseline for REE on EL 23848 and, unexpectedly, two further target styles in ground previously explored only for gold. Our priority is to confirm REE potential at the complex margin and follow up the new targets to gain better understanding of what may be there."

Figure 1. EL 23848 soil survey on the project geology, showing the Billabong Complex margin target (R1) and the two new target areas (T1 and T2). Coordinates GDA2020 MGA zone 52.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/10047/324696_620aa6b4f4e3bb68_002full.jpg

REE results

REE are highest along the south-west margin of the complex, where five consecutive samples on one line (R1) returned 85–112 ppm TREO, all in the top 15% of the survey. Absolute levels are low and dominated by light REE (heavy REE are about 13% of the total), and thorium rises with REE at the margin, so part of the response is lithological. The Company sees the spatial link to the margin as a positive first step, and the key follow-up objective is to test whether heavy-REE-enriched zones exist beneath the cover, which the wide line spacing could not resolve.

Previously unrecognised targets

T1 lies 1.5–2.3 km north-west of the complex margin. Arsenic, tellurium, molybdenum and copper rise together over four consecutive samples and give way over the next four to an antimony peak of 0.55 ppm, about 2.3 times the survey median, with palladium elevated over the first part of the zone. Gold is low (survey maximum 3.1 ppb), consistent with earlier work, so T1 is a pathfinder response and not a gold anomaly; the same suite marks gold systems in ultrafine surveys elsewhere in Australia. T2 lies about 1.5–2.4 km outside the margin and combines copper (to 50 ppm), sulphur, palladium and platinum with a chromium-nickel peak, a pattern seen over mafic-ultramafic rocks. Amplitudes at both targets are modest and need confirmation.

Figure 2. Gold and copper maps with the approximate Billabong Complex outline: survey-wide Au and Cu with targets T1 and T2 outlined, and zooms of the T1 pathfinder zone and the T2 copper response. Gold is low (maximum 3.1 ppb); T1 is a pathfinder response.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/10047/324696_620aa6b4f4e3bb68_003full.jpg

Next steps

Follow-up will confirm the REE signal and test the two new targets in parallel, using low-cost methods before any drilling is considered. Results will determine which targets, if any, advance to drill testing.

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Sigma Lithium was recognized at COP31, the United Nations Climate Change Convention, for sustainability innovation with circularity in lithium production at its Cleantech Industrial Plant. 

  • Sigma Lithium's participation at COP31 marks the Company's seventh consecutive COP, where its pioneering sustainable business model in critical minerals was highlighted.

    • At COP31, Co-Chair and CEO Ana Cabral delivered a keynote presenting "The Circular Advantage" at the World Climate Summit.

    • Since COP25 in Madrid in 2019, Sigma Lithium has been recognized for its sustainable lithium by UN world leaders in COP26-Glasgow, COP27-Sharm el-Sheikh, COP28-Dubai, COP29-Baku, COP30-Belém and now COP31-Antalya.

  • The Company reprocesses its dry-stacked tailings fines producing 23% more lithium from the same ore mined:

    • Generates additional revenue from high-grade and low-grade lithium fines, without additional mining.

    • Recovering more lithium per tonne mined reduces waste and the environmental footprint per tonne of product.

    • Lower operating risk by design: tailings are dry-stacked with no tailings dams, and 90% of process water is reused.

    • Sigma Lithium's circular production model, upcycling dry-stacked tailings, responds to growing circularity and traceability expectations from battery supply chains, including in the EU.

  • Built for battery supply-chain requirements: 100% renewable electricity and zero use of hazardous chemicals, as battery makers face growing scrutiny of how their raw materials are produced.

  • Safe, reliable operations: more than 1,190 consecutive days without a lost-time injury and a 2026 year-to-date Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate of zero, as at November 10, 2026.

  • COP31 caps a year of global recognition of the Company's sustainability leadership, including being selected by Nasdaq to ring the Closing Bell at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on September 22, 2026, during United Nations Climate Week.

    • Sigma Lithium has pioneered the large-scale industrialization of critical minerals in Brazil, capturing value in the Jequitinhonha Valley and delivering a 32% gross margin in 3Q 26.

  • Response to media reports: Sigma Lithium denies recent media reports and reaffirms that its mining rights and concessions are in good standing with ANM and the competent authorities. The matter is being addressed through the regular procedures under Brazilian law.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Sigma Lithium Corporation (NASDAQ: SGML) (ASX: SAU) (TSXV: SGML) (BVMF: S2GM34) ("Sigma Lithium" or the "Company"), the largest producer of industrial-mineral lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas¹, has presented results from the circular cleantech model at its Grota do Cirilo operation in Minas Gerais, Brazil, at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye: a plant that industrializes 23% more lithium from the same ore mined, stores its tailings without dams and reuses 90% of its water.

These results are built into how the plant runs and how it makes money. Reprocessing tailings fines adds saleable product and revenue without additional mining. Dry-stacking removes the need for a tailings dam and the long-term risk that comes with one. Renewable power and zero hazardous chemicals respond to growing customer scrutiny of how battery raw materials are produced.

Ana Cabral, Co-Chair and CEO, said: "COP31 reaffirmed that the energy transition will be built on critical minerals produced responsibly, at scale and with full transparency. Sigma Lithium is proud to demonstrate, from Brazil to the world, that circularity and clean technology can unlock the full value of critical minerals.

"Investors and customers increasingly want evidence of how critical minerals are produced, not pledges. Our circular model shows that responsible production and better economics go together: the same plant that reuses its water and keeps its tailings out of dams also gets more lithium from every tonne we mine. Industrializing lithium where it is mined keeps more of the value in Brazil, and our Sustainability Report will put this performance on the record, open to scrutiny."

KEY SUSTAINABILITY ACHIEVEMENTS PRESENTED AT COP31

At the World Climate Summit, Ana Cabral delivered the keynote "The Circular Advantage: Unlocking Critical Minerals Value Through Clean Technology," presenting how Sigma Lithium, the largest producer of industrial-mineral lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas, combines large scale, low cost and sustainability. Key messages included:

100% Circularity: Cleantech Industrial Plant 3.0 upcycles tailings fines through industrial reprocessing into high-grade and low-grade lithium fines, generating additional revenues and delivering 23% more lithium industrialized from the same ore.

Innovation-Driven Operations: SCADA algorithms enable self-learning metallurgy from mineralogy and real-time detection and correction of anomalies, while a new automated reprocessing circuit for tailings creates additional production capacity.

Environmental Stewardship: 90% water reuse, 100% renewable electricity, zero use of hazardous chemicals and tailings dry-stacking. A two-pit mine design preserves the Piauí Creek as a water source for the community, and active germination of rock piles integrates them with the landscape.

Top Global Safety Record: More than 1,190 consecutive days without a injury and a 2026 year-to-date Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR) of zero.

Social Development Engine: More than 19,600 job positions supported — 1,350 at Sigma Lithium, 14,800 indirect positions across the supply chain, more than 2,000 through the Microcredit Program for Women and 1,400 through the Irrigation Program for Small-Scale Agriculture — benefiting more than 78,400 family members in one of Brazil's most disadvantaged regions.

Value Creation in Producing Regions: Ethically sourced critical minerals are exported as industrialized materials — oxides or concentrates — with significant value added captured by the producing region. Sigma Lithium's Cleantech Industrial been delivering robust gross margins by transforming ore into lithium oxide concentrate, showing how industry will propel Latin America to develop its critical minerals. All the elements are already in place in the Jequitinhonha Valley: power, infrastructure and roads.

RECOGNITION FOR SUSTAINABILITY LEADERSHIP AT UNITED NATIONS CLIMATE CHANGE CONVENTION COP31 - SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE COP

Attending COP31, the United Nations Convention on Climate Change in Antalya, caps a year of global recognition for Sigma Lithium's sustainability leadership. On September 22, 2026, during United Nations Climate Week in New York, the Company was selected by Nasdaq to ring the Closing Bell at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, in recognition of its pioneering role in sustainable critical minerals.

COP31 was Sigma Lithium's seventh consecutive COP since COP25 in Madrid in 2019. The delegation, led by Ana Cabral, took part in the Future of Mining Coalition roundtable with the World Climate Foundation, the World Climate Summit, a Future of Cities session with Instituto Orbis, the United Nations and CNI, and IBRAM and CNI's Essential Minerals for the Energy Transition Coalition during Minas Day.

RESPONSE TO MEDIA REPORTS

Sigma Lithium is aware of recent inaccurate media reports and reaffirms that its mining rights and concessions granted by Brazil's National Mining Agency (ANM) remain in force.

The Company is currently handling the case within the regular procedures provided under Brazilian legislation, including the right to defense and subsequent stages with the competent labor authorities.

The Company will continue to address the matter with the appropriate authorities, in accordance with legal procedures and its commitment to ethical, responsible conduct guided by respect for laws and people.

As one of the main employers in the Jequitinhonha Valley, the Company contributes to the generation of jobs, income and opportunities, in addition to the economic and social development of the region.

ABOUT SIGMA LITHIUM

Sigma Lithium Corporation (NASDAQ: SGML) (ASX: SAU) (TSXV: SGML) (BVMF: S2GM34) ("Sigma Lithium" or "the Company") is the largest industrial-mineral producer of lithium oxide concentrate in the Americas¹ and is dedicated to industrializing socially and environmentally sustainable lithium materials to supply global producers of batteries for energy security. The Company runs one of the world's largest lithium production sites—the fifth-largest industrial-mineral complex for lithium oxide concentrate—at its Grota do Cirilo operation in Brazil. Sigma Lithium currently has a nameplate capacity to industrialize 330,000 tonnes of lithium oxide concentrate on an annualized basis at its mine and state-of-the-art Cleantech Industrial Plant.

Sigma Lithium is at the forefront of environmental and social sustainability in the battery materials supply chain. Its Cleantech Industrial Plant combines 90% water reuse, zero use of toxic chemicals, no tailings mud dams, and 100% renewable electricity. For more than three years, Sigma Lithium has recorded no lost-time accidents.

The Company plans to resume its Phase 2 expansion in 2027, which is designed to nearly double annual production capacity to 580,000 tonnes. It also plans a Phase 3 expansion to increase capacity further to 830,000 tonnes. For more information about Sigma Lithium, visit our website.

PARSIPPANY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Zoetis Inc. (NYSE: ZTS) today announced that the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has licensed Poulvac® Procerta® HVT-ND-ILT, a vector vaccine for chickens. The license marks an important milestone in Zoetis’ continued investment and industry leadership in poultry health, disease protection, and innovation. Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT brings three disease targets together in one vaccine and expands the tools available to poultry veterinarians and producers as they develop vaccination programs.

“The USDA license is an important achievement for our poultry business and reflects Zoetis’ commitment to advancing practical solutions for customers,” said Abhay Nayak, Executive Vice President and President, U.S. Commercial Operations at Zoetis. “Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT adds a new option to our portfolio, giving veterinarians and producers more flexibility to tailor their vaccination strategies. Our team looks forward to working with customers as they consider how it may support their flock-health programs.”

3-in-1 protection veterinarians can count on

ILT remains an economically significant respiratory disease, with outbreaks capable of causing significant losses in flocks. 2 Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT is designed to provide early, long-lasting protection against Marek’s disease (MD), Newcastle disease (ND) and infectious laryngotracheitis (ILT). 1 It is labeled for administration to healthy one-day-old chickens or 18- to 19-day-old embryonated chicken eggs.

More flexibility in vaccination programs

Zoetis’ poultry vaccine portfolio gives veterinarians options to build vaccination programs around flock needs and disease challenges. Poulvac Procerta HVT-ND-ILT can be included in seasonal or rotational ILT programs that also use modified-live vaccines. It complements other Poulvac® hatchery and immune-complex vaccines designed to address additional disease challenges, including infectious bursal disease, infectious bronchitis, Salmonella and E. coli.

Support beyond the vaccine

Zoetis poultry specialists support customers by helping plan and implement targeted vaccination programs that optimize bird health and well-being. Tailored support can include technical guidance, diagnostic testing and analysis, hatchery services and team training, as well as vaccine audits and flock-health assessments.

About Zoetis

Zoetis is the world’s leading animal health company, driven by a singular purpose: to nurture our world and humankind by advancing care for animals. With a legacy of nearly 75 years, Zoetis continues to pioneer ways to predict, prevent, detect, and treat animal illness, supporting veterinarians, livestock producers, and pet owners in over 100 countries. Key Terms

vector vaccinetechnical
A vaccine that uses a harmless virus (a viral vector) as a delivery vehicle to carry genetic instructions for a disease-causing protein (antigen) into human cells; those cells then produce the antigen so the immune system learns to recognize it. Vectors can be engineered so they cannot replicate, or left replication‑competent in a controlled way, and the body's immune response may target both the antigen and the vector itself, which can affect repeat dosing or vaccine effectiveness.
modified-live vaccinesmedical
Vaccines that use live microorganisms (viruses or bacteria) that have been weakened or genetically altered so they can replicate only to a limited degree in the body and no longer cause the disease they would in an unvaccinated person. Because the modified organism can briefly reproduce, these vaccines tend to produce a strong, broad immune response similar to natural infection; however, they are not the same as inactivated (killed) or subunit vaccines and are generally unsuitable for people with severely weakened immune systems or other specific medical contraindications.

Partnership combines WebMD ONE, a trusted engagement platform, with Dario's comprehensive AI-powered multi-condition platform and clinical care solutions to help employers, health plans and health systems translate engagement into measurable health outcomes and in-year healthcare cost savings

Revenue contribution to Dario to begin in 2027

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DarioHealth Corp. (NASDAQ: DRIO), a leading AI-powered healthcare technology company transforming the management of chronic conditions, today announced a strategic partnership with WebMD Health Services, one of the industry's leading well-being and population health organizations serving more than 3,500 employers, health plans, health systems and public sector organizations.  Dario expects the partnership to begin contributing annual recurring revenue ("ARR") in 2027, including via distribution through the administrative services organization ("ASO") of a leading integrated healthcare system serving a broad network of hospitals and healthcare services.

The partnership brings Dario's comprehensive multi-condition whole-person care platform to the WebMD ecosystem, combining WebMD's trusted risk identification, engagement and behavior change capabilities with Dario's clinically validated care programs, provider backed care, and DarioIQ, its AI-driven intelligence engine that uses proprietary longitudinal health data to personalize member engagement and interventions. These capabilities are designed to help organizations convert member engagement into meaningful clinical outcomes while addressing multiple health needs through a single integrated platform.

Through the partnership, WebMD Health Services will offer Dario's full suite of integrated solutions, including cardiometabolic care, behavioral health, musculoskeletal care with posture management, obstructive sleep apnea ("OSA"), women's health, including perimenopause and menopause support, GLP-1 support programs and access-to-care capabilities through Dario's provider network.

"This partnership with WebMD brings together the key growth drivers we have been building across Dario," said Erez Raphael, Chief Executive Officer of Dario. "WebMD Health Services is a trusted partner that gives us the opportunity to introduce our solutions to employers and health plans across its client base, which represents millions of lives. As clients choose to add Dario, our multi-condition platform creates the opportunity to deliver multiple solutions through each new customer relationship. DarioIQ enables us to personalize engagement at scale, and our provider-backed care capabilities extend our role further into the care journey. Together, these capabilities create a powerful model for expanding both our reach and revenue as we partner with the leading name in health and well-being."

The collaboration enables organizations already leveraging WebMD Health Services to seamlessly connect members from WebMD ONE into personalized clinical interventions across multiple chronic conditions, creating a more unified approach to whole-person health while reducing the complexity of managing multiple point solutions and delivering improving return on investment ("ROI") and healthcare cost savings. A recent independent analysis of published peer-reviewed studies confirmed that Dario's platform has the potential to reduce total healthcare costs for payers by up to 10% in-year.  

"We're committed to delivering outcomes-based solutions that help our clients reduce risk and manage costs, while improving the health and well-being of their populations," said John Harrison, President and General Manager of WebMD Health Services. "Our partnership with Dario builds on the cost containment solutions already available through WebMD ONE and gives organizations another way to address risk where it matters most. By connecting engagement with personalized clinical support at a higher level of clinical acuity, clients can achieve measurable outcomes and more effective cost management across a broad range of health needs."

The partnership represents another milestone in Dario's strategy of delivering its AI-powered, whole-person care platform through premier ecosystem partners, making comprehensive digital health more accessible while helping organizations improve outcomes, enhance member experiences and maximize the value of their well-being and health investments.

Phase 1 data presented in an oral plenary session at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics (ENA 2026) in Barcelona, Spain, showed deep and durable responses in patients with FGFR3-altered urothelial cancer (UC) and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). As of the data cutoff in the ongoing study, 6 of 10 evaluable patients with FGFR3 activating alterations treated at doses of ≥3.3 mg/kg had responded, including 3 of 5 with UC and 3 of 3 with HPV-positive HNSCC.

  • Responders to BHV-1530 in UC included patients who failed prior enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (EV+P) and oral FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. All responders remained on treatment at data cutoff, some beyond 6 months.

  • BHV-1530 was well tolerated with no FGFR class toxicities: no DLTs, treatment-related SAEs or deaths, and no ILD; no hyperphosphatemia, nail dystrophy or central serous retinopathy.

  • Biohaven completed FDA Type C meeting in 4Q 2026 and plans to initiate a pivotal study evaluating BHV-1530 in FGFR3-altered tumors, starting with UC, expected to begin as early as 1H 2027 to support potential accelerated approval.

BARCELONA, Spain and NEW HAVEN, Conn., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Biohaven Ltd. (NYSE: BHVN) ("Biohaven"), a global clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development and commercialization of life-changing therapies to treat a broad range of rare and common diseases, today announced clinical data from the ongoing Phase 1 study of BHV-1530, its first in class potential FGFR3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with a novel topoisomerase I (TopoIx) payload. The data were presented today by Gerald S. Falchook, M.D., Director of Sarah Cannon Research Institute at HCA HealthONE, in an oral presentation during Plenary Session 3 at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics (ENA 2026) in Barcelona, Spain. As of the October 19, 2026 data cutoff, 30 patients had received BHV-1530 monotherapy every three weeks (Q3W) at doses from 1.0 to 12.0 mg/kg, and dose escalation is ongoing. Patients had received a median of two prior lines of therapy for advanced disease, and all patients with UC had progressed on EV+P.

Among 10 efficacy-evaluable patients with activating FGFR3 alterations, treated with BHV-1530 at doses of 3.3 mg/kg or higher, 9/10 had a tumor reduction and 6 achieved a partial response (PR; confirmed or unconfirmed, by investigator assessment per RECIST v1.1; Figure 1). Responses were observed in tumors with FGFR3 mutations and fusions, including in 3 of 5 patients with UC and all 3 patients with HPV-positive HNSCC. All responders remained on treatment as of the data cutoff, some for more than 6 months.

Gerald S. Falchook, M.D. commented, "Many patients in this study had progressed on multiple prior therapies, including enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab and FGFR inhibitors in urothelial cancer, so seeing durable responses is very encouraging." Dr. Falchook added, "We also saw deep responses in HPV-positive head and neck cancer, where options after immunotherapy are limited. Importantly, BHV-1530 has been well tolerated, with no dose-limiting toxicities and none of the hyperphosphatemia, nail or retinal toxicities that often restrict FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy."

In UC, where all patients had progressed on prior EV+P, partial responses occurred in 3 of 5 patients with FGFR3-altered tumors, including a patient who had also received a prior FGFR inhibitor. Tumor reductions were also observed in the 2 patients with FGFR3 wild-type tumors, including one partial response pending confirmation (Figure 2).

Dr. Falchook presented the clinical case of a patient with HPV-positive metastatic HNSCC and an FGFR3 S249C mutation, who had received four prior lines of therapy including chemoradiation, a platinum doublet and immunotherapy. This patient achieved a confirmed partial response, with a 67% reduction in target lesions at Week 6 that deepened to 86% by Week 24, (Figure 3) and remains on therapy beyond 6 months with no treatment-related adverse events. This case illustrates the speed and depth of response in a highly refractory patient who failed prior standard of care.

BHV-1530 was well tolerated across all dose levels in 30 patients, with no dose-limiting toxicities, treatment-related serious adverse events or treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events, nausea (43%) and fatigue (37%), were all Grade 1 or 2. Hematological toxicity was mostly low grade and manageable. None of the toxicities that commonly limit FGFR inhibitor therapy (hyperphosphatemia, nail dystrophy or central serous retinopathy) were observed, and no interstitial lung disease (ILD) was reported. Pharmacokinetic data showed that BHV-1530 is highly stable in circulation, with free payload exposure below 1% of ADC exposure, and a half-life of 7 to 14 days that supports Q3W dosing.

Nushmia Khokhar, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of Oncology at Biohaven stated, "Unlike FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which block kinase signaling inside the cell, BHV-1530 is an ADC designed to bind FGFR3 on the tumor cell surface, be internalized and release a potent topoisomerase I payload, independent of kinase-domain resistance mutations."

Dr. Khokhar added, "Following a recent Type C meeting with the FDA, we are excited to advance BHV-1530 into a pivotal study in FGFR3-altered tumors, beginning with urothelial cancer, as early as the first half of 2027, with the goal of supporting a potential accelerated approval."

FGFR3 is frequently altered or overexpressed in UC. Activating mutations or fusions, together with overexpression of the wild-type receptor, are found in about half of metastatic UC and in 70% to 80% of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, and are also seen in head and neck, lung and other solid tumors (Figure 4). Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab is now the first-line standard of care for advanced UC, but many patients eventually progress and options after progression remain limited. The only FDA-approved FGFR-targeted therapy for advanced UC is an oral pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), indicated only for previously treated patients whose tumors carry a susceptible FGFR3 alteration, which leaves patients whose tumors overexpress wild-type FGFR3 without a targeted option. Pan-FGFR TKIs also inhibit FGFR1, FGFR2 and FGFR4, and their labeled class effects include hyperphosphatemia, nail disorders, stomatitis and retinopathy, which often require dose interruptions or reductions. Resistance can also emerge through mutations in the kinase domain where these drugs bind. BHV-1530 is designed to bind FGFR3 on the tumor cell surface rather than inhibit its kinase, and is being studied in patients with and without FGFR3 alterations.

BHV-1530 takes a different approach to FGFR3 than approved pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which block kinase signaling across the FGFR family (Figure 5). The investigational antibody-drug conjugate is designed to bind selectively to FGFR3 on the tumor cell surface and deliver its TopoIx payload inside the cell, with no detectable binding to FGFR1, FGFR2 or FGFR4 in preclinical studies.

About Study BHV1530-101

BHV1530-101 (NCT06874335) is a Phase 1, first-in-human, multicenter study of BHV-1530 as monotherapy and in combination with an anti-PD-1 antibody in adults with advanced solid tumors. Patients with UC, HNSCC or non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were enrolled irrespective of FGFR3 alteration status, without a minimum FGFR3 expression threshold. Patients with other solid tumors were eligible if their tumors harbored an activating FGFR3 alteration.

About BHV-1530

BHV-1530 is an antibody-drug conjugate directed against FGFR3, a validated but underexploited target in urothelial cancer and other FGFR3-driven cancers and is a first-in-class potential FGFR3-directed ADC incorporating Biohaven's proprietary TopoIx payload. Unlike approved FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which are restricted to genomically selected patients and constrained by class-related toxicities, BHV-1530 is designed to target FGFR3 with the potential to address both FGFR3-altered and wild-type overexpressing tumors. BHV-1530 is being studied in an ongoing Phase 1 dose-escalation trial in unselected patients with advanced urothelial cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and non-small cell lung cancer who have failed standard-of-care therapy, as well as other tumor types harboring FGFR3 genomic alterations. Biohaven has initiated combination cohorts evaluating BHV-1530 with anti-PD-1 therapy, including the combination with LIBTAYO® (cemiplimab) which is now enrolling.

About Biohaven

Biohaven Ltd. (NYSE: BHVN) is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of life-changing treatments in key therapeutic areas, including immunology, neuroscience, and oncology. Biohaven is advancing its innovative portfolio of therapeutics, leveraging its proven drug development experience and multiple proprietary drug development platforms. Biohaven's extensive clinical and preclinical programs include Kv7 ion channel modulation for epilepsy; MoDE™ and TRAP™ extracellular protein degradation for immunological diseases; and myostatin inhibition for neuromuscular and metabolic diseases, including obesity. Fourth-Quarter Results

Revenue was up 7.1% (or 7.5% in constant currency). Consistent with prior quarters, Recorded Music revenue growth was unfavorably impacted by the termination of the distribution agreement with BMG (the “BMG Termination”), which resulted in $7 million less Recorded Music digital revenue compared to the prior-year quarter. Excluding the BMG Termination, total revenue was up 7.5% (or 7.9% in constant currency).

Digital revenue increased 13.2% (or 13.1% in constant currency) and streaming revenue increased 13.7% (or 13.5% in constant currency). Recorded Music streaming revenue increased 13.4% (or 13.2% in constant currency); however, adjusted for the $7 million impact of the BMG Termination, Recorded Music streaming revenue was up 14.3% (or 14.0% in constant currency) driven by continued market growth, including upside from price and wholesale rate increases, as well as market share gains. Music Publishing streaming revenue increased 15.1% (the same in constant currency). Revenue increases in the quarter were also driven by growth in Recorded Music physical and licensing revenue, partially offset by lower Recorded Music artist services and expanded-rights revenue and Music Publishing performance and mechanical revenue. Music Publishing synchronization revenue remained constant.

Operating income increased by $177 million to $320 million in the quarter from $143 million in the prior-year quarter, primarily due to revenue mix and a $107 million decrease in restructuring and non-cash impairment charges compared to the prior-year quarter, and a $7 million decrease in amortization expense, as well as factors affecting Adjusted OIBDA discussed below, partially offset by a $21 million increase in non-cash stock-based compensation costs due to accelerated expense recognition associated with executive transition and involuntary terminations coupled with higher vesting expense of outstanding awards.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 17.8% from $405 million to $477 million (or 17.2% in constant currency) and Adjusted OIBDA margin increased 2.1 percentage points to 23.8% from 21.7% (or 1.9 percentage points from 21.9% in constant currency), primarily driven by strong operating performance, revenue mix and savings from the Company’s restructuring plans, a portion of which has been reinvested into the Company’s business.

Net income increased by $70 million to $179 million from $109 million in the prior-year quarter. The increase was primarily due to the factors affecting operating income described above, and the impact of exchange rates on the Company’s Euro-denominated debt resulting in a gain of $7 million compared to a loss of $1 million in the prior-year quarter, partially offset by a loss of $1 million on intercompany loans compared to a gain of $13 million in the prior-year quarter. The increase was also partially offset by a tax expense of $98 million in the quarter compared to a benefit of $3 million in the prior-year quarter driven by higher pre-tax income and tax expense recognized in connection with a change in our indefinite reinvestment assertion.

Basic and Diluted earnings per share were $0.34 for both the Class A and Class B shareholders due to net income attributable to the Company in the quarter of $179 million.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company reported a cash balance of $589 million, total debt of $4.704 billion and net debt (defined as total debt, net of deferred financing costs, premiums and discounts, minus cash and equivalents) of $4.115 billion, compared to $3.833 billion at the end of the prior year. Total debt as of September 30, 2026 includes $303 million of subsidiary debt acquired in the Company’s acquisition of Tempo Music Holdings, LLC (“Tempo Music”) and $363 million in loans outstanding under the Beethoven JV. The debt is secured only by certain music rights owned by Tempo Music and the Beethoven JV, respectively, and is nonrecourse to the Company and its subsidiaries, other than Tempo Music and the Beethoven JV, respectively.

Cash provided by operating activities decreased 32% to $158 million from $231 million in the prior-year quarter. The decrease was largely the result of timing of working capital, including the timing of payments related to the Company’s restructuring plans and contractual digital advances, partially offset by strong operating performance. Capital expenditures decreased to $25 million, from $28 million in the prior-year quarter. Free Cash Flow, as defined below, decreased $70 million to $133 million from $203 million in the prior-year quarter.

Full-Year Results

Total revenue increased 10.9% (or 8.9% in constant currency). As previously disclosed, Recorded Music revenue growth was impacted by a $12 million digital revenue settlement in the year and $4 million for performance obligations satisfied in previous periods in the prior year (the “DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments”) as well as $16 million in digital revenue from the settlement of certain infringement cases in the prior year (the “Copyright Settlement”). In addition, revenue growth was unfavorably impacted by the BMG Termination, which resulted in a $29 million decrease in Recorded Music digital revenue compared to the prior year. Music Publishing revenue was impacted by $17 million of revenue in the prior year recognized in connection with the historical matched royalties that were processed to date by the Mechanical Licensing Collective (the “MLC Historical Matched Royalties”). Adjusted for these items, total revenue was up 11.8% (or 9.8% in constant currency).

Digital revenue increased 12.5% (or 10.4% in constant currency) and streaming revenue increased 13.4% (or 11.2% in constant currency). Recorded Music streaming revenue increased 13.5% (or 11.1% in constant currency). Adjusted for the impact of the DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments of $12 million in the current year and $4 million in the prior year, and the impact of the BMG Termination of $29 million in the prior year, Recorded Music streaming revenue increased 14.2% (or 11.8% in constant currency) driven by continued market growth, including upside from price and wholesale rate increases, as well as market share gains. Music Publishing streaming revenue increased 13.0% (or 11.5% in constant currency). Adjusted for the $17 million impact of the MLC Historical Matched Royalties, Music Publishing streaming revenue increased 15.5% (or 13.9% in constant currency). Revenue increases in the year were also driven by growth in Recorded Music artist services and expanded-rights, physical and licensing revenue and Music Publishing performance, synchronization and mechanical revenue.

Operating income increased by $483 million to $1,177 million from $694 million in the prior year. The increase in operating income was primarily due to revenue mix, savings from the Company’s strategic restructuring plans, a portion of which has been reinvested in the Company’s business, and factors that led to the increase in Adjusted OIBDA discussed below, partially offset by a $25 million increase in amortization expense and a $9 million increase in depreciation expense.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 22.7% to $1,770 million from $1,443 million (or 19.4% in constant currency). Fourth-Quarter Results

Recorded Music revenue was up 6.8% (or 7.3% in constant currency), driven by growth across digital, physical, and licensing revenue, partially offset by a decrease in artist services and expanded rights revenue. Excluding the $7 million impact of the BMG Termination in the prior-year quarter, Recorded Music revenue increased 7.3% (or 7.8% in constant currency). Digital revenue was up 12.9% (or 12.8% in constant currency), and streaming revenue was up 13.4% (or 13.2% in constant currency). Adjusted for the $7 million impact of the BMG Termination, Recorded Music streaming revenue was up 14.3% (or 14.0% in constant currency). Streaming revenue reflects growth in subscription revenue of 14.9% (or 14.7% in constant currency), and in ad-supported revenue of 9.1% (or 8.6% in constant currency). Subscription revenue, adjusted by $3 million for the BMG Termination, increased 15.4% (or 15.2% in constant currency). Ad-supported revenue, adjusted by $4 million for the BMG Termination, increased 11.0% (or 10.5% in constant currency). The increase in subscription revenue reflects continued market growth, including upside from price and wholesale rate increases, as well as market share gains and other items such as audits and accruals, including the impact of a $7 million DSP audit payment for historical periods. The increase in ad-supported revenue reflects market share gains in the quarter as well as improved deal economics. Physical revenue increased 28.5% (or 30.5% in constant currency) primarily driven by strong releases in the quarter. Licensing revenue increased 11.9% (the same in constant currency), due to an increase in licensing deals. Artist services and expanded-rights revenue decreased 21.4% (or 19.9% in constant currency) attributable to higher merchandising revenue in the prior-year quarter, primarily from the Company’s partnership with Oasis. Major sellers in the quarter included Madonna, Number_i, Charli XCX, Bruno Mars and Linkin Park.

Recorded Music operating income increased $157 million to $365 million, up from $208 million in the prior-year quarter and operating margin was up 8.7 percentage points to 22.3% versus 13.6% in the prior-year quarter. The increases in operating income and operating income margin were driven by revenue mix, a $75 million decrease in restructuring and non-cash impairment charges compared to the prior-year quarter and a $10 million decrease in amortization expense, as well as the factors affecting Adjusted OIBDA discussed below.

Adjusted OIBDA increased 19.2% (or 18.8% in constant currency), to $423 million from $355 million in the prior-year quarter, and Adjusted OIBDA margin was up 2.7 percentage points to 25.8% from 23.1% in the prior-year quarter (or 2.5 percentage points from 23.3% in constant currency). The increases in Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin were primarily driven by revenue growth and strong operating performance, and savings from the Company’s restructuring plans, a portion of which has been reinvested in the Company’s business.

Full-Year Results

Recorded Music revenue was up 10.7% (or 8.7% in constant currency), driven by growth across digital, artist services and expanded-rights, physical and licensing revenue. Excluding the impacts of the DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments of $12 million in the current year and $4 million in the prior year, and the impact of the BMG Termination of $29 million and the Copyright Settlement of $16 million in the prior year, Recorded Music revenue was up 11.5% (or 9.5% in constant currency). Digital revenue was up 12.4% (or 10.1% in constant currency), largely driven by growth in streaming revenue of 13.5% (or 11.1% in constant currency), partially offset by a decrease in download and other digital revenue of 29.2% (or 30.0% in constant currency). Streaming revenue reflects growth in subscription revenue of 14.8% (or 12.4% in constant currency) and in ad-supported revenue of 9.5% (or 7.5% in constant currency). Subscription revenue, adjusted for the impacts of the DSP True-Up and Settlement Payments of $12 million in the current year and $4 million in the prior year, and the impact of the BMG Termination of $18 million in the prior year, increased 15.4% (or 12.8% in constant currency). The increase in subscription revenue reflects market growth, including upside from price and wholesale increases, market share gains and strong chart performance, and the increase in ad-supported revenue reflects market share gains and an overall strong performance in the year as well as improved deal economics. Physical revenue increased 12.5% (or 11.5% in constant currency) driven by strong releases in the year as well as catalog and carryover success. Supplemental Disclosures Regarding Non-GAAP Financial Measures

We evaluate our operating performance based on several factors, including the following non-GAAP financial measures:

Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin

We allocate resources and evaluate performance based on several factors, including Adjusted OIBDA. We define Adjusted OIBDA as operating income (loss) adjusted to exclude the following non-operational, discrete, or non-cash items to facilitate period-over-period comparability: (i) non-cash depreciation of tangible assets, (ii) non-cash amortization of intangible assets, (iii) non-cash stock-based compensation and other related expenses, (iv) gains or losses on divestitures, (v) expenses related to restructuring, impairment, and transformation initiatives, which include costs associated with the Company’s financial transformation initiative to design and implement new information technology and upgrade our finance infrastructure, and (vi) executive transition costs. We define Adjusted OIBDA margin as Adjusted OIBDA as a percentage of revenue. Items excluded are not viewed to contribute directly to management’s evaluation of operating results. We consider Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin to be important indicators of the operational strengths and performance of our businesses. However, a limitation of the use of Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin as performance measures is that they do not reflect the periodic costs of certain capitalized tangible and intangible assets used in generating revenues in our businesses. Accordingly, Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for, operating income (loss), operating income (loss) margin, net income (loss) attributable to Warner Music Group Corp. and other measures of financial performance reported in accordance with United States generally accepted accounting principles (“U.S. GAAP”). In addition, our definitions of Adjusted OIBDA and Adjusted OIBDA margin may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies.

Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS

We define Adjusted Net Income as net income (loss) attributable to Warner Music Group Corp. adjusted to exclude the following non-operational, discrete, or non-cash items to facilitate period-over-period comparability: (i) non-cash amortization of intangible assets, (ii) expenses related to restructuring and transformation initiatives, which include costs associated with the Company’s financial transformation initiative to design and implement new information technology and upgrade our finance infrastructure, (iii) gains or losses on divestitures, (iv) non-cash stock-based compensation, (v) loss on extinguishment of debt, (vi) executive transition costs, (vii) other (income) expenses, and (viii) certain discrete tax items. Excluding the impact of certain discrete tax items, these exclusions are then further adjusted to account for tax effects. Adjusted Net Income should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for, net income (loss) attributable to Warner Music Group Corp. and other measures of financial performance reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP. We use Adjusted Net Income to calculate Adjusted Earnings (Loss) Per Share (“EPS”), which we define as Adjusted Net Income divided by the basic weighted-average shares outstanding for the period. Our definition of Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS may differ from similarly titled measures used by other companies.

CALGARY, AB, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Northstar Clean Technologies Inc. (TSXV: ROOF) (OTCQB: ROOOF) (" Northstar"" or the " Company ") is pleased to announce that it will host a virtual investor webcast on Tuesday, December 1, 2026, to provide a comprehensive production and operational update on its Empower Calgary facility ("Empower Calgary" or the "Facility"), alongside a review of the Company's third quarter 2026 financial results.

As part of the webcast, Northstar will introduce a series of key operating metrics designed to provide shareholders with greater transparency into production performance, facility maintenance and ongoing optimization activities. The Company intends to report these metrics on an ongoing basis throughout the Facility's ramp-up, after which time it will reassess its reporting measures to ensure they remain relevant to its evolving operations.

The update will include a detailed review of recent production activity, operational achievements and areas for continued improvement, including the Company's ongoing efforts to enhance facility reliability as it advances the ramp-up toward commercial production.

Management will also discuss production performance in relation to previously achieved milestones, and the ongoing balance among processing operations, equipment improvements and maintenance during the Facility ramp-up.

"Transparency and accountability are important to us as we continue the ramp-up of Empower Calgary," said Aidan Mills, President & CEO of Northstar. "We recognize that shareholders want greater visibility into our production performance, the challenges we are addressing and the progress we are making. The operating metrics we plan to introduce are the measures I want our team to be evaluated against, and we believe they will provide a clearer and more consistent basis for assessing our performance and improvements over time."

Q3 2026 Financial Results and Investor Webcast

Northstar intends to file its unaudited interim financial statements and management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, on November 30, 2026.

The Company will host a virtual investor webcast on December 1, 2026, to discuss these financial results and provide the comprehensive production update outlined above. Management will also address investor questions during the webcast.
